items.title: AnyVar MCP Server
items.text: Variation data for AI agents. This prototype connects an AnyVar service to MCP-compatible hosts. Its tools let agents register supported variant nomenclature, retrieve GA4GH VRS objects, search regions, and follow available mappings.

items.title: Who is this for?
items.text:
• Agent developers building research or variant-curation workflows in an MCP-compatible host.
  • Researchers and curators who need answers tied to VRS identifiers and AnyVar responses.
  • Teams running AnyVar that want to offer agent access through defined tools.

items.title: Get started
items.text:
• Quickstart walks through preparing AnyVar, installing the MCP package, connecting an AI agent, and using the tools.
  • Dependencies covers starting and checking AnyVar.
  • Configuration lists the MCP server settings.
  • Connect your AI agent to the MCP server.
  • Contributing explains development setup.

items.title: Configuration
items.text: Set these values through environment variables or a .env file. Environment variables take precedence. Omitted settings use the defaults below.

items.title: AnyVar HTTP Service connection
items.text:
Choose the AnyVar service to contact and limit how long HTTP connections and response reads can wait.

Setting Default Description ANYVAR_API_URL http://localhost:8000 Base URL of your AnyVar service. ANYVAR_API_TIMEOUT 10 seconds Timeout for the HTTP connection and each response read.

items.title: Registration
items.text:
Control whether agents can write to AnyVar.

Setting Default Description ANYVAR_ENABLE_REGISTRATION false Allow registration to write objects to AnyVar.

items.title: Search and response limits
items.text:
Limit the cost of broad searches and the amount of data returned to agents. The response size limit applies to all tools.

Setting Default Description ANYVAR_SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE 100 results Search page size when page_size is omitted or null, from 1 to 10,000. ANYVAR_MAX_SEARCH_SPAN 1000000 positions Maximum width of a search interval, including both bounds. ANYVAR_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES 1048576 bytes (1 MiB) Maximum response size accepted from AnyVar. Larger responses return an error.

If a search page exceeds the response limit, lower the page size before starting a new search. Keep the effective page size unchanged when following continuation cursors. Raise the response size limit if larger objects or pages are needed.

items.title: Request budgets
items.text:
Guard against accidental agent loops and request bursts. Each server process has its own budget, so these limits do not enforce a shared AnyVar service quota.

Setting Default Description ANYVAR_MAX_CALLS_PER_MINUTE 30 Maximum AnyVar calls per server process in a rolling minute. ANYVAR_MAX_CALLS_PER_HOUR 500 Maximum AnyVar calls per server process in a rolling hour.

A request must fit within both rolling windows.

items.title: Set configuration values
items.text:
For Claude Desktop or Codex CLI, set environment variables in the agent's MCP configuration as shown in Connect your AI agent.

If you use a .env file, place it in the MCP server process's working directory:

ANYVAR_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
ANYVAR_API_TIMEOUT=10
ANYVAR_ENABLE_REGISTRATION=true

items.title: Connect your AI agent
items.text:
Install anyvar-mcp and start the AnyVar HTTP API. Keep the API running while you use the tools. Claude Desktop or Codex CLI starts anyvar-mcp using the command you configure below.

Set the environment variables in the examples to your values if you want to override the defaults. See the configuration guide.

items.title: Find the server command
items.text:
Find the executable:

command -v anyvar-mcp

If nothing prints, activate the virtual environment where you installed the server and try again. Save the printed path. Use it as the command if your agent cannot find anyvar-mcp. For a virtual environment, it might look like:

/home/git/anyvar-mcp/.venv/bin/anyvar-mcp

items.title: Claude Desktop
items.text:
1. Open Settings → Developer → Edit Config to find claude_desktop_config.json.
  2. Add this entry to mcpServers, keeping any existing server entries:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "anyvar-mcp": {
      "command": "anyvar-mcp",
      "env": {
        "ANYVAR_API_URL": "http://localhost:8000",
        "ANYVAR_ENABLE_REGISTRATION": "true"
      }
    }
  }
}

If Claude Desktop cannot find the command, replace the command value with the full executable path.

  1. Save the file, fully quit Claude Desktop, and reopen it.
  2. In a new chat, open Add files, connectors, and more → Connectors → Manage connectors and select anyvar-mcp to check its tools.

See the Claude Desktop MCP documentation for more setup options and troubleshooting.

items.title: Codex CLI
items.text:
For example, add the MCP server with ANYVAR_API_URL set to http://localhost:8000 and ANYVAR_ENABLE_REGISTRATION set to true:

codex mcp add anyvar-mcp --env ANYVAR_API_URL=http://localhost:8000 --env ANYVAR_ENABLE_REGISTRATION=true -- anyvar-mcp

Confirm that the saved server list includes anyvar-mcp:

codex mcp list

See the Codex MCP documentation and CLI reference for more configuration options and commands.

items.title: Config file
items.text:
Edit the server's environment variables in ~/.codex/config.toml:

[mcp_servers.anyvar-mcp.env]
ANYVAR_API_URL = "http://localhost:8000"
ANYVAR_ENABLE_REGISTRATION = "true"

items.title: CLI
items.text:
Inspect the current entry, remove it, and add it again with all settings you want to keep. For example, to change the API URL and disable registration:

codex mcp get anyvar-mcp
codex mcp remove anyvar-mcp
codex mcp add anyvar-mcp --env ANYVAR_API_URL=http://localhost:9000 --env ANYVAR_ENABLE_REGISTRATION=false -- anyvar-mcp

items.title: Check tools from the terminal
items.text:
With Node.js and npx installed, you can use the MCP Inspector to list tools independently of your agent:

npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli anyvar-mcp --method tools/list

Once connected, try the tools.

items.title: Contributing
items.text: This page explains how to set up the project for development, run tests, and update the documentation.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
You will need:

  • Python 3.13 or newer
  • Git
  • A terminal or command prompt

items.title: Set up a virtual environment
items.text:
If you are not a repository maintainer, first fork the repository on GitHub. Then clone your fork (or the main repository if you have access), enter its directory, and create a virtual environment:

Replace OWNER with your GitHub username for a fork, or genomicmedlab for the main repository.

git clone https://github.com/OWNER/anyvar-mcp.git
cd anyvar-mcp
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

items.title: Install the development dependencies
items.text:
Install the package in editable mode with development, test, and documentation dependencies. Editable mode makes changes in src/ available without reinstalling:

python3 -m pip install -e '.[dev,tests,docs]'

items.title: Install the pre-commit hooks
items.text:
Install the hooks after installing the development dependencies:

prek install

items.title: Style checks
items.text:
Check style with ruff:

python3 -m ruff check --fix .
python3 -m ruff format .

items.title: Tests
items.text:
Run unit and integration tests:

python3 -m pytest

Mark tests that require a running AnyVar service or external resources with @pytest.mark.live.

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
Edit the Markdown files in docs/. Preview the site locally:

zensical serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8001.

Build the site with the same strict checks used in CI:

zensical build --clean --strict

items.title: Open a pull request
items.text:
Run the checks relevant to your changes, review the generated documentation, and open a pull request on GitHub. Include a short summary of the change and any relevant testing or documentation notes.

If the pull request resolves an issue, say so with a closing keyword such as Closes #123, where 123 is the issue number. GitHub will close the issue automatically when the pull request merges. If the pull request is related to an issue but does not resolve it, use a non-closing reference such as Refs #123, where 123 is again the issue number, or link the issue through the pull request's GitHub interface instead.

items.title: Start the AnyVar HTTP API
items.text: The MCP server uses AnyVar's HTTP API to register and retrieve variants. Follow AnyVar's setup instructions to start the HTTP API. Keep it running while you use the MCP tools.

items.title: AnyVar compatibility
items.text: This MCP server targets AnyVar commit ec3c765. Other versions may return different responses or lack required endpoints. Check your service's version at /service-info before using the examples.

items.title: Check the AnyVar HTTP API
items.text:
Follow these steps to check that the AnyVar HTTP API is running correctly and can register a variant.

Set ANYVAR_API_URL to your service's base URL. Run these commands in the same terminal:

export ANYVAR_API_URL="http://localhost:8000"

Request service information:

curl --fail-with-body "${ANYVAR_API_URL%/}/service-info" \
  | python3 -m json.tool --indent 2

Expected response excerpt:

{
  "id": "org.biocommons.anyvar",
  "name": "AnyVar",
  "type": {
    "group": "org.biocommons",
    "artifact": "anyvar",
    "version": "1.0.1.dev196+gec3c7651b"
  }
}

The full response also includes service metadata, supported data standards, and dependency information. Check the version against the supported AnyVar commit.

Ensure AnyVar service is running

If the request fails, check the URL and that the service is running. Open the service's base URL in a browser to view its API documentation.

items.title: Register a variant
items.text:
Register a sample variant to check processing and storage:

curl --fail-with-body --request PUT "${ANYVAR_API_URL%/}/variation" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"definition": "NC_000010.11:g.87894077C>T"}' \
  | python3 -m json.tool --indent 2

Expected registration response:

{
  "input_variation": {
    "definition": "NC_000010.11:g.87894077C>T",
    "assembly_name": "GRCh38"
  },
  "messages": [],
  "object": {
    "id": "ga4gh:VA.K7akyz9PHB0wg8wBNVlWAAdvMbJUJJfU",
    "type": "Allele",
    "digest": "K7akyz9PHB0wg8wBNVlWAAdvMbJUJJfU",
    "location": {
      "id": "ga4gh:SL.01EH5o6V6VEyNUq68gpeTwKE7xOo-WAy",
      "type": "SequenceLocation",
      "digest": "01EH5o6V6VEyNUq68gpeTwKE7xOo-WAy",
      "sequenceReference": {
        "type": "SequenceReference",
        "refgetAccession": "SQ.ss8r_wB0-b9r44TQTMmVTI92884QvBiB"
      },
      "start": 87894076,
      "end": 87894077
    },
    "state": {
      "type": "LiteralSequenceExpression",
      "sequence": "T"
    }
  },
  "object_id": "ga4gh:VA.K7akyz9PHB0wg8wBNVlWAAdvMbJUJJfU"
}

Return to the quickstart to install and connect the MCP server.

items.title: Quickstart
items.text: Only local MCP server connections over stdio are currently supported. Your AI agent starts the MCP server when it connects.

items.title: Watch the demo
items.text: Codex CLI using GPT-6-Luna at low reasoning effort

items.title: Prepare AnyVar
items.text: Start the AnyVar HTTP API and keep it running while you use the MCP tools. Note its base URL for the connection settings below.

items.title: Install the MCP server
items.text:
Install from PyPI:

python3 -m pip install anyvar_mcp

items.title: Connect your AI agent
items.text: Follow Connect your AI agent with ANYVAR_API_URL set to your AnyVar service's base URL. Enable ANYVAR_ENABLE_REGISTRATION=true to run the registration example below. See Configuration for all settings.

items.title: Verify the connection
items.text:
With anyvar-mcp connected, check that your host shows its tools:

  • Claude Desktop: Open a new chat. The server's tools should be available through Add files, connectors, and more → Connectors.
  • Codex CLI: Run codex and enter /mcp. You should see anyvar-mcp: connected (4 tools).

items.title: Use the tools with your AI agent
items.text: Send the prompts below to your connected AI agent to explore the tools, register a variant, retrieve its mappings, and search a genomic region. Follow the examples in the same conversation so the agent can refer to earlier results. Each example describes what to expect; the agent's wording may vary.

items.title: See what tools are available
items.text:
What tools are available through the AnyVar MCP server?

The response should list the available tools with a brief description of each.

items.title: Check supported nomenclatures and identifiers
items.text:
Which variant nomenclatures or identifier formats does each tool support?

The response should describe the accepted inputs for each tool, distinguishing variant expressions, VRS identifiers, and genomic region inputs.

items.title: Register a variant
items.text:
Send this request in the chat or Codex prompt:

Use the AnyVar MCP to register NC_000010.11:g.87894077C>T and tell me about the response.

Registration writes to AnyVar

Approve the tool call if your host asks. Registration requires ANYVAR_ENABLE_REGISTRATION=true in the server configuration.

When registration succeeds, the response should include a VRS Allele object and its identifier, along with any messages or warnings.

items.title: Retrieve mappings
items.text:
Ask the agent to explain variant mappings, then retrieve them for the registered variant:

Explain what variant mappings represent in AnyVar, then retrieve the registered variant and list its available outgoing mappings.

The response should briefly explain mappings and their direction, then show the registered VRS object and its outgoing mappings, or indicate that none are stored.

items.title: Inspect mapped objects
items.text:
If a mapping is returned, ask to see both objects:

Show me the full VRS objects for that mapping.

The response should include the full source and destination VRS objects for the selected mapping.

items.title: Search a region
items.text:
To try region search, send:

Search the registered variants on chromosome 10 from 87894070 through 87894080, inclusive. Show the IDs.

The response should list VRS IDs for registered variants found in the interval, or indicate that none were found in the registry.
